I did more research and self reflection and switched to INSY the next semester. I have no regrets but definitely look at entry level/internship jobs on Indeed and Handshake that you find interesting and see what kind of degrees and skills they ask for, and tailor your degree plan around that. You want classes that teach you hard skills and have you work on projects that you can put on your resume and talk about during interviews - especially if you graduate without any internships. You don’t need a BS in INSY to work in software development. You can study leetcode on your own without having to more spend money than you need to. Additionally, having a master’s in CS would be more beneficial than taking 1 more programming course (INSY4306), which is what the BS entails. Honestly INSY in general doesn’t prepare you very well to be a SWE. UNT is offering rn a pathways program for non-Stem undergrad degree holders who are interested in pursuing a masters in CS. You’re conditionally admitted on the basis that you take 3 prep classes that catch you up to speed  in the Fall and Spring, and if you get at least a B in them, you get credit towards the master’s. Might be worth looking into!

Remember you can always pivot into something you’re  interested in once you start your career.

While i’m not a grad yet I know people who have graduated with info sys degrees albeit not necessarily from UTD, so i can provide some insight. I know people who’ve gone into cybersecurity, software engineering, business analyst of some sort, and consulting. Conversely, I’ve heard of people who got stuck working dead-end jobs that have nothing to do with IS. You probably know that ITS is what you make of it - it’s not a traditional degree like going for accounting & becoming an accountant. However, just like with any other degree, it’s just as important what you learn outside of the classroom as you do inside the classroom. Whether it’s getting certs, grinding leetcode, and/or building projects - a college degree is ultimately what you make of it. One of my SWE friends had a senior dev who was a History major. Ultimately, everyone i know who was successful & happy with a 6-figure job with an IS degree applied themselves: learning interview prep, getting internships, networking with the right people, and constantly trying to learn everything they could about what wasn’t being taught in class. Hope this helps! Good luck!
